findings.title: The impersonation -> uuid step of the extracted gate order is unmeasured: hoisting the id check above the whole gate survives
findings.reason: M03 moved requireOperatorProposalWriter's `if (!z.uuid().safeParse(id).success) return errorResponse('proposal_not_found', 404)` above `await requireOperatorWriter(sql, request)`, and the apply-route case `POST apply returns 404 operator_disabled before auth when the flag is off` PASSED. The mutant is not behaviour-preserving: with the Operator flag OFF a malformed proposal id now answers `proposal_not_found` instead of `operator_disabled`, and an impersonated session with a malformed id answers 404 instead of the 409 `impersonation_not_allowed` that gate.ts:70-79 and docs/directory/app-api-b.md:86 both document as coming first. Nothing can see it, because the repository never combines the two inputs: both malformed-id cases pass the flag ON with no impersonation cookie (apply-route.test.ts:187, decline-route.test.ts:113), and every refusal case passes a valid uuid (apply-route.test.ts:77 and :111, decline-route.test.ts:62, and all three gate.test.ts cases, which call requireOperatorWriter and never requireOperatorProposalWriter at all -- the proposal-writer wrapper introduced by 99975e2e9 has no direct test). Remedy, two cases in gate.test.ts: call requireOperatorProposalWriter with `OWNER_OPERATOR_ENABLED=false` and `params: Promise.resolve({ id: 'not-a-uuid' })` and assert `operator_disabled`; then with the `rw_impersonation` cookie and the same malformed id and assert 409 `impersonation_not_allowed`.

findings.title: The Receipt's `before` can be swapped for the after-state and the whole suite stays green -- the only assertion that reads it is an absence-of-key proxy
findings.reason: M22 changed the new buildReceipt helper's `before: parseVoiceState(proposal.before, 'agent_proposals.before')` to `before: afterActual` and the live-DB case `worker-produced proposals render and apply successfully` PASSED. That case is the ONLY place in the repository that reads a server-built Receipt's `before`, and what it asserts is `expect(result.proposal.receipt.before).not.toHaveProperty('updatedAt')` (apply.integration.test.ts:606) -- an absence-of-key proxy that `toVoiceState(committed)` satisfies just as well, because toVoiceState (apply.ts:528-536) projects exactly the five VoiceState fields and drops `updatedAt`. Nothing else covers the field: apply.test.ts reads only `actorName` and `actorUserId` off the written Receipt (apply.test.ts:206, :209) and uses a hand-built FIXTURE receipt for the repeat-Apply case (apply.test.ts:238-257); apply.integration.test.ts:283-299 asserts nine Receipt fields but not `before`; ProposalCard.test.tsx renders a fixture Receipt; there is no ReceiptView test file at all. The field is owner-visible -- ReceiptView renders before/after, and the glossary plus plan decision P6 pin it as `the state the card SHOWED when the owner clicked`. Remedy is one line, e.g. `expect(receipt.before).toEqual(parseVoiceState(view.before, 'agent_proposals.before'))` at apply.integration.test.ts:606, or `expect(receipt.before.tone).toBeNull()` beside the existing `after.tone` assertion at apply.integration.test.ts:283.
findings.arbiter_reasoning: EXECUTED: buildReceipt runs on the happy path this case drives, and the case reads `receipt.before` directly, so the mutated expression is neither dead nor on an untaken branch. NOT EQUIVALENT, proven from the case's own fixture: the location is seeded with an unset tone and the case asserts `expect(await readTone(locationId)).toBe('warm and brief')` after the Apply (apply.integration.test.ts:610), so `proposal.before.tone` is null while `afterActual.tone` is 'warm and brief' -- the mutant writes a materially different document into `agent_proposals.receipt`. NOT a no-op-on-this-input mutation and not a spelling change. Therefore a confirmed survivor, recorded as survived-confirmed-P0 rather than `inconclusive` (the branch IS executed) or `equivalent` (behaviour is provably NOT preserved).

findings.title: `withPatchedProposal` -- the card-repaint half of Apply/Not now re-rendering from the returned row -- is executed by no test
findings.reason: M25 reduced `turn.proposals.map((p) => (p.id === row.id ? row : p))` to `turn.proposals.map((p) => p)`, making `patchProposal` a no-op, and the OperatorClient case `terminal failures and requested capabilities survive reload and subsequent turns` PASSED. Reverse import search: useOperatorConversation is imported only by OperatorClient.tsx, useProposalWrites.ts and useTurnPoll.ts; the single suite that renders OperatorClient is OperatorClient.test.tsx, and it never activates a card write -- its only reference to the Apply control asserts that two such buttons exist (OperatorClient.test.tsx:579). The new useProposalWrites.test.tsx passes `patchProposal` in as a `vi.fn()` (useProposalWrites.test.tsx:43), so the real implementation is never reached from there either, and ProposalCard.test.tsx drives the card with props rather than the hook. The two halves of the property the handoff asks about are therefore split: useProposalWrites really does hand the server's row to `patchProposal` (proved by M12), but what the transcript does with it is unverified. Remedy: one OperatorClient case that clicks Apply against a routed 409 carrying a `proposal` row and asserts the card's state line changed, or a direct renderHook test of useOperatorConversation's `patchProposal`.

findings.title: The handoff's gate citation is wrong in both halves: neither the SHA nor the fingerprint matches the recorded evidence
findings.reason: The bullet reads `Review gate GREEN at 79f695d53 (fingerprint 1545d93f...)`. Re-resolved against HEAD: .feature/codex-gate-fingerprint.json records `headSha 3082da75f97b94a4c82e7ed2468b22ac90103480`, `generatedAt 2026-09-12T20:51:20.344Z` and `fingerprint a2f7363f4dd9f4eb56f42d8d9aa6504e229fd31b5095d93b572f4654499bd60b`; .feature/gate-status.json carries `"mode":"full"` (not `review`) at the same timestamp with `reclassify` WARN and every other check PASS; .feature/state.json records `lastGreenGateSha 3082da75f97b94a4c82e7ed2468b22ac90103480`. `3082da75f` is the docs-only handoff commit, authored 2026-09-12T13:48:13-07:00, i.e. AFTER 79f695d53 (13:29:45-07:00) and before the gate ran. `rg '1545d93f'` over the whole worktree matches only this sentence -- the value appears in no artifact it claims to cite. P1 and not P0 because the claim is directionally true (the gate is green, and 3082da75f's `src` tree is byte-identical to 79f695d53's, so no code was gated unverified); it is the identifiers a resumed session is told to check that are false. Remedy: cite `a2f7363f...` at `3082da75f`, mode `full`.

findings.title: The new card-write suite hardcodes a wording sentence the same commit un-exported, against wording.ts's own stated rule
findings.reason: useProposalWrites.test.tsx:132-134 asserts the literal 'Something went wrong. Nothing was changed - try again.', while line 120 of the same file asserts through the imported constant (`ROUTE_ERROR_WORDING.proposal_stale`). The literal exists because commit 79f695d53 dropped `export` from ROUTE_ERROR_FALLBACK (wording.ts:204) as part of the fallow dead-code sweep, so the new suite cannot import the one constant it needs. wording.ts:143-148 states the rule this breaks in its own words: spelling a sentence twice `let the live answer and the stored record drift apart, which is the same reason PROPOSAL_STALE is a constant (F4)`. Kept at P2, not P1: the assertion pins the correct words, so it fails on drift rather than passing through a bug -- it is a maintenance trap, not a fake assertion. Remedy: assert `routeErrorSentence(null)`, which is still exported, instead of the literal.

findings.title: `useTurnSubmission` returns a fresh object every render while both sibling hooks memoize -- the one decomposition product that skipped the file's own stability rule
findings.reason: Sibling search over the three machines the commit split apart: useOperatorConversation ends in `useMemo` (useOperatorConversation.ts:397-414) and useTurnPoll ends in `useMemo` (useTurnPoll.ts:167-170), but the new file-local useTurnSubmission returns a bare object literal (OperatorClient.tsx:254-263). `submission` therefore changes identity on every render and `startNewConversation`'s `useCallback(..., [conversation, poll, submission])` (OperatorClient.tsx:330) is re-allocated every render. Harmless at HEAD -- OperatorClient declares no `useEffect`, so no dependency array consumes `startNewConversation`, which is why this is P2 -- but this exact file carries a scar from the same class of bug: OperatorClient.test.tsx:17-22 hoists ONE router object because an unstable one made `a response that triggers a state update ... an infinite read loop (RB2-06)`. Remedy: wrap useTurnSubmission's return in `useMemo`, matching its two siblings.
